card.name: Words after a historical subject
card.fires_on: Words right after a named person, group or institution in historical or encyclopedic prose, such as a possessive, verb or article. It marks the spot where the text goes on to say what that subject made, founded or owned.

modes.label: Possessive or article after a subject
modes.description: A word like their, the, 's or a that follows a group or place and leads into a noun about what it owned or did.
modes.example: He and Sarah changed their name to Lawrence and Thomas Edward was the second of<< their>> five In 1907

modes.label: Founding or building verb
modes.description: A verb of creating or establishing right after a ruler or founder.
modes.example: In 1143 Vladislav II<< founded>> Strahov Monastery, the second

card.writes: Weak output effect; it promotes a mix of odd name pieces like Convenience, Fresh and Stokes.
card.plain: It lights up on small words after a historical figure or group, just before the text says what they built or founded.
